title: West Virginia Paranormal Trail returns with 1 new stop & new prizes
excerpt: The West Virginia Department of Tourism has announced the return of the statewide Paranormal Trail, which is designed to showcase the state’s most haunted locations.
content:
BRIDGEPORT, W.Va (WDTV) - The West Virginia Department of Tourism has announced the return of the statewide Paranormal Trail, which is designed to showcase the state’s most haunted locations.

A digital passport will allow visitors of each location to check in, earn points and unlock prizes, including a glow-in-the-dark sticker, custom beanie, adventure-ready lantern and limited-edition poster.

Travelers can register to participate in The West Virginia Paranormal Trail online and instantly receive the digital passport via email or text, organizers said.

From local legends to historic haunts, the trail now highlights 20 eerie landmarks across West Virginia:

  • The Trans-Allegheny Lunatic Asylum, with its Gothic architecture and dark history, is a popular destination for paranormal enthusiasts wanting to experience the chilling atmosphere firsthand. The site has been featured on SyFy’s Ghost Hunters and the Travel Channel’s Ghost Adventures.
  • Known for ongoing paranormal activity, the West Virginia Penitentiary offers a somber exploration of its haunted history. The penitentiary has even been featured in TIME Magazine.
  • As the first ghost tour in America, this tour is rooted in Harpers Ferry’s haunted history. The Ghost Tour of Harpers Ferry is a spine-tingling journey uncovering unearthly tales of the town’s former residents.
  • Dedicated to the legend of the Mothman, the Mothman Museum offers a glimpse into the sinister sightings near the “TNT Area.”
  • Dedicated to the infamous 1952 sighting, the Flatwoods Monster Museum offers a comprehensive look into this eerie event and other paranormal phenomena in West Virginia.
  • With its ominous atmosphere and reported paranormal activity, the Old Hospital on College Hill attracts ghost hunters from far and wide. The site was even featured on the Travel Channel’s Destination Fear. 
  • Haunted by the apparition of “The Colonel,” a Civil War officer with a long beard, the Historic Glen Ferris Inn provides a unique and memorable experience.
  • Led by experienced tour guides, the Shepherdstown Mystery Walk is a unique and immersive journey through Shepherdstown’s most haunted historical sites.
  • The Shepherdstown Ghost Tours are a candlelit experience that is equal parts history lesson and haunted tale.
  • The Haunted Haymond delivers a frightening adventure with spooky scenes and creepy characters. This 130-year-old house provides a petrifying experience for thrill-seekers of all ages.
  • A chilling relic of the B&O Railroad era, the Flinderation Tunnel, positioned on the North Bend Rail Trail, is rumored to be haunted by the spirits of its builders, attracting paranormal enthusiasts to uncover its eerie history. 
  • Along the Elk River Trail between Ivydale and Duck, you’ll find a 10.5-foot, 1,800-pound Bigfoot looming in front of you. This towering figure was crafted by students in Clay County.
  • The West Virginia Bigfoot Museum in Sutton is home to the largest mid-Atlantic collection of casts, hair samples, research and documented Bigfoot sightings.
  • Silver Run Tunnel #19 on the North Bend Rail Trail in Cairo is rumored to be haunted by a spectral figure of a woman in white.
  • Cryptid Mountain Miniature Golf in Morgantown is an indoor mini-golf course with 13 cryptid-themed holes.
  • Hempfield Tunnel in Wheeling is believed to be haunted by the souls of those buried beneath its tracks.
  • Apollo Civic Theater in Martinsburg was alive with stage acts and roaring applause in 1914; it’s believed that some of the performers have never truly left.
  • Carnegie Hall in Lewisburg is one of only four Carnegie Halls in the world still in use. Built in 1902 after a mysterious fire consumed the original Lewisburg Female Institute, there have been reports of unexplained footsteps, flickering lights, and spectral whispers. 
  • Greenbrier Valley Theater, also in Lewisburg, hosts The Greenbrier Ghost, one of the many interpretations of the local Greenbrier County legend, where the trial of Zona Heaster Shue’s murder in 1897 was won based on the testimony of a ghost.

The new spooky stop:

  • Droop Mountain Battlefield State Park in Hillsboro is a Civil War battlefield turned state park that ranks among the region’s most haunted locations, with ghostly encounters reported throughout its grounds.

Some other locations that were previously on the Paranormal Trail, but are now not listed on the website, include:

  • As one of the oldest hotels in the state, the Blennerhassett Hotel has its share of ghost stories, with hallways said to be haunted by ghostly children playing tag and men in top hats.
  • Haunted by the spirits of those who perished there, Lake Shawnee Abandoned Amusement Park delivers an eerie experience in a desolate, forgotten setting.
  • Rumored to be a hotspot for paranormal activity, Hotel Morgan is a boutique hotel that blends luxury with history — and perhaps a few hauntings.
  • Seneca Caverns in Riverton has long been known as a gathering place for Native Americans; these vast underground chambers are said to hold secrets, and perhaps spirits, that linger in the shadows.

The 2026 pass will expire on December 31, 2026. If you have registered in previous years, you will need to register again for the 2026 challenge.

The prize-winning milestones include checking in at:

  • three or more spots to receive the sticker
  • eight or more spots to receive the beanie
  • 15 or more spots to receive the lantern
  • All spots will receive a limited-edition poster and a chance for the grand prize.

The grand prize winner will be announced in January 2027, and the winner will receive a gift certificate valid for an overnight tour at the Trans-Allegheny Lunatic Asylum for two.

For more information on West Virginia’s Paranormal Trail or to register for a digital passport, visit wvtourism.com/paranormal.
